<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dbe4eea09949cb37da86cc24870d2527d70c4b86` — the merge of head `4a1e80ae7c59d7181b3dffaf9347edc785c54fbd` into base `6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dbe4eea09949cb37da86cc24870d2527d70c4b86 && git checkout dbe4eea09949cb37da86cc24870d2527d70c4b86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 4a1e80ae7c59d7181b3dffaf9347edc785c54fbd && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672 && git merge --no-ff 4a1e80ae7c59d7181b3dffaf9347edc785c54fbd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6a40a09ed952f83b1f765d47cd76aee4a41f6672` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

CI red, not this PR's · `domain:engine` seat 2 (#20966) · `os-steve` · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` · 2026-10-12T05:54Z.

- **What failed:** `Test Core (6/6)` → "Check this shard's timing drift" on head `10f3b686f4` (run `38208219378`): `2990.7s measured vs 1855.5s predicted across 12 package(s) = 1.61x`. Every other step of the shard is green: 12 of 12 packages reported, and all 20068 tests are accounted for.
- **Why it is not this PR's:** the overshoot sits in packages this diff does not touch: `runtime` 1.75x, `service-analytics` 2.17x, `rest` 1.46x, `plugin-approvals` 1.74x and `client` 1.70x. Two other PRs that change packages low in the graph went red on the same step at the same ratio (PR #22953 at 1.60x, PR #22959 at 1.62x), while `main`'s runs since the 2026-10-12 dataset refresh are green. Filed fresh as #22966.
- **Fix:** none exists yet. The step forbids hand-editing the dataset or raising its 1.5x bound, so the remedy is #22966's to route.
- **Re-run:** this seat has no means to re-run a job. The relay carries no re-run op. The patch round in progress on this PR (the caller census row and the i18n bundles) is not asked to touch this step. Its own reds on the earlier head are its work, and this one is not. A head that is green apart from this step waits on #22966 for arming. It still gets its contract review, which this step does not block.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f21b6f9d24483ad9ff10b1b8bef00008347758ca`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed: card #22877 (body and all 13 comments; ruling 6116165299 binding), PR #22954 (body, both comments, the 24-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `e357a441c6`, and patch round 1 alone, `288ef6fb69..f21b6f9d24`), the head's check-runs, and the `origin/main` files the brief lists. The file list touches no governed path; this is the contract-tier review the ruling asked for the migration half.

**Gates on the head, at the final read:** 42 check-runs, none pending (the second `PR Automation` run's `Check Changeset` had completed `success`). 40 are green or skipped, every required context among them except `Test Core`. Two are red, both the open-card signatures and not this diff's: `Test Core (6/6)` is red at the step "Check this shard's timing drift" only — "Run this shard's tests" and "Test completeness guard" on that shard are `success` (#22966); the `Test Core` aggregator is red at "Check the per-package suite-duration ceilings" and its "Verify test shard results" roll-up only (#22949). The three reds of head `288ef6fb69` — `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Type Check · consumer gates` — are green on this head, the four i18n steps of the consumer gates included.

### ① Derived judgments

Each judged against ruling 6116165299 (letter A, Q2 i), on the diff and the `origin/main` code it lands in.

- **The member column — right.** `SysMetadataObject` gains `bundle_member`, nullable text, `maxLength` 100, documented as written from the body and never authored. `overlayMemberValue` answers `undefined` for every type outside `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS`, and every caller — `whereFor`, the row payload in `put`, `overlayMemberWhere`, `historyRowsOfMember` — adds the column only when that answer is defined, so a name-only type's reads and writes are byte-identical (CONTROL pinned in `sys-metadata-repository.bundle-member.test.ts` over every payload and every `where`; the backfill case pins every other type's rows equal, all columns). NULL is the one spelling of the canonical member: `overlayMemberValue` folds `en-US`, an empty value and a missing value to `null`, so a pre-column row and a post-column row of one member cannot sit under two keys. The additive schema sync (`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`) provisions the column on a table that booted before; a store whose sync did not run fails its first member-keyed read or write loudly, and the backfill reports at `error` with the fix.

- **The declared index and both runtime partial indexes — right, with one residual to state.** The declared `idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active` gains the column; `OVERLAY_INDEX_COLUMNS` and `OVERLAY_NULL_SENTINELS` gain it, folded to the empty string the way `package_id` is, so `overlayIndexKeyParts`, `buildOverlayIndexSql` (active and draft), `buildOverlayFallbackIndexSql` and `buildOverlayDuplicateProbeSql` read one key (pinned as literals in `overlay-index.test.ts`). The ceremony is `probeThenReplaceIndex`, unchanged: the new form is built under the probe name over the live data and dropped, and only then is the real name dropped and rebuilt. A store that booted before holds the four-part partial index; the five-part key is a strict relaxation of it, so no row that index admitted can fail the probe, and the real-SQLite pin starts from the four-part index and watches it replaced. The one row set that can still block is the one #6418 already reports — two package-less active rows distinct only by a NULL `package_id` under the declared, never-migrated index — and the `conflict` arm reports it exactly as before. `syncDeclaredIndexes` skips by name, so the five-column declaration never replaces the live four-part index by itself; the ceremony does, lazily, at the first protocol write (`ensureOverlayIndex`, reached from the eight write doors), not at boot — a member insert through a path that bypasses those doors before any protocol write would meet the old index once, loudly. The SQL drift planner cannot misread the result: `isSyncReproducibleIndex` answers false for any partial index, so the five-part runtime index is runtime-managed and never a drift op. **A driver without partial indexes (the fallback arm, MySQL):** the probe fails `unsupported`, the non-unique composite fallback is added without a drop, and the degradation report names the dialect (its text now names canonical members too). On such a store that booted before, the four-column declared UNIQUE stays under the name, so a second member's save — an INSERT under the new write head — is refused by that index: loud, where before it merged silently; `os migrate plan` lists the declaration change as a destructive `recreate_index` for the operator. A fresh store there gets the five-column declared UNIQUE and two members coexist. The survival pin is therefore delivered on the ceremony's dialects, where the pins run (real SQLite, the showcase); on the fallback dialect the defect changes shape from silent replacement to a refused save. That is the ceremony's standing scope, which the ruling chose, and not a breach — but neither the PR body nor the changeset states it; the seat should add the sentence.

- **The backfill — right.** `backfillOverlayBundleMembers` runs through the engine (`find` by `type`, `update` by `id`, as system), over the discriminated types only and in every organization; skips a row that already carries a member (idempotent, pinned); parses the body and writes only a non-canonical member. A row whose body has no locale is left NULL: `itemDiscriminator` answers the canonical `en-US` for a missing field, `overlayMemberValue` folds it to `null`, nothing is written — the ruling's "NULL means the canonical member" and the schema's own default. An unparseable body is counted and left NULL. It runs from `loadMetaFromDb` once the hydration read has answered, and from `ensureOverlayIndex` before the first write, once per protocol instance; it never throws; a missing table is benign through `isMissingTableError`; any other failure is an `error`-level report naming the consequence and the fix, retried at the next boot. Its order against the index rebuild is free, as the module says: the new key only relaxes the old one.

- **The repository — right; one member, never a sibling.** `put` takes the member from the body through `overlayMemberOfBody`, never from a caller; `resolveWriteHead` narrows the inherited-draft base, the head lookup and the orphan-draft adoption to it; the row payload carries the column only when defined, on insert and update alike. `get`, `headAt`, `delete`, `promoteDraft` (the draft read, the active parent read, the `put`, and the drain — `dropPromotedDraftRow` receives the option bag whole, so the member it was promoted from reaches the delete), `restoreVersion` (refuses a version whose history body belongs to another member with `404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, and reads the active row by member) and `history` (`historyRowsOfMember`: a row's member from its body, a tombstone's from the row it removed via `previous_checksum`; an unstamped parent or an unparseable body reads as canonical) all address one member; omitted means canonical. Pinned on the repository alone, the cross-member revert refusal and the member-scoped drain included.

- **The save door — right.** `saveMetaItem` hands `itemDiscriminator` of the body to `storedHeadAt` for its parent-version resolution and to the credential carry-forward (`storedBodyForCarryForward`), so the head the optimistic lock judges is the row `put` will key; both derive from the same body.

- **By-name reads and deletes with no selector — right.** `findServedOverlayRow` adds `overlayMemberWhere` (canonical) for a bundled type and nothing for every other type; the publish door's draft read and the diff door's history rows (`historyRowsOfMember`) and active row address the canonical member; `deleteMetaItem` pre-reads through `repo.get` and deletes through `repo.delete`, both canonical by default; the history door (`repo.history`) and the revert doors (`repo.restoreVersion`) default to canonical. `getMetaItem` canonicalises `request.type` at its head, so the new block's discriminator lookup sees the singular. When only a non-canonical member is overlaid, a bare `getMetaItem` finds no canonical stored row and serves the code layer's canonical member through `lookupArtifactItem` (`getArtifactItem` is canonical-first inside each tier, independent of registration order); only a bundle that ships no canonical member at all falls to the registry's bare read, which answers its overlay tier first — and there no canonical member exists to answer. Pinned: the package wording for a `zh-CN`-only customisation, before and after a restart. The ruling's premise that the registry's bare read already answers the canonical member is false by `SchemaRegistry.getItem`'s own code (bare tier before local and other; canonical-first only inside a tier); the dev implemented the operative half at the protocol and left `registry.ts` alone, as the claim required. One note: `overlayLockLayerAt` still gathers every active row of the name and reduces to the strictest lock document — a protection envelope, never a body, in the conservative direction; unchanged by this diff and acceptable.

- **The shared version counter (the seat's Q2 answer A) — right.** `nextItemVersion` is per `(organization, type, name)` from the maximum in `sys_metadata_history`, and that table declares `unique (organization_id, type, name, version)`, so a per-member counter would collide or need a second ceremony on a second table. With `history` filtered by member, the diff door filtered the same way, `restoreVersion` refusing a sibling's version, and `revertCommit` items restoring under the canonical member (a commit item recorded for a non-canonical member answers 404 there rather than restoring the wrong member), no history or revert path reaches a sibling member's snapshot. The visible cost is non-consecutive version numbers within one member. A faithful reading of "the version counter carries the member": what that sentence protects holds.

- **Patch round 1 (three commits, +247/−14 over 13 files) — right.**
  - `operatorFacingErrorText` in the backfill's catch: kept, with its census row (`calls: 1`) and a sentinel pin in `raw-exec-operator-detail-16657.test.ts` for both legs (`find` with the synthetic bound statement; `update` binding the row id, which is the sentinel). The helper's answer reaches exactly two carriers — the result's `detail` and the `logProblem` report — and both are pinned sentinel-free with the dialect's words intact; the success line carries a count only, and `ensureOverlayMembersBackfilled` discards the result. The sentinel leaks nowhere. Keeping the call is right: the engine-level backfill has no enumerated reporting site, and the helper is the one cut.
  - The seven regenerated `platform-objects` bundles: `en` rewritten from the source; the three translated locales carrying the English text with their source-hash companions recording the fill — the generator's documented merge mode; `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-stale-fill` and `check:i18n-coverage` are green on the head.
  - The pre-flight: `buildOverlayMemberPresenceSql` (a zero-row select of the column) and `buildOverlayDuplicateProbeSqlWithoutMember` (grouped by the other four key parts, the member projected as the constant empty key) live in `overlay-index.ts`; `runProbe` tries the presence statement — no result set reads `unreadable`, as every statement there is judged; a refusal selects the member-less listing — and reports the statement that ran as the entry's `duplicateSql`. A pre-column store cannot answer anything other than its true state under the key the rebuild will judge: every row there is the empty member, so grouping by the other four parts IS the five-part grouping of that table — no under-report is possible, and the groups are the ones the full statement would find. The one over-report is the strict case the dev names: a discriminated-type pair whose bodies name different locales, which the serving boot's backfill separates. Report shape: `RuntimeIndexPreflight`'s keys are unchanged (`status`, `groups`, `duplicateSql`, `keyParts`, `detail`); group keys are built generically from the row's columns, so `bundle_member_key` appears inside `groups[].key` on every listing, full and member-less alike; the CLI consumer (`duplicates.ts`) reads `status` and `rowCount`, and its contract and integration tests are green in `Test Core (3/6)`. A presence-probe failure other than a missing column also routes to the member-less statement; on a post-column store that could list a legitimate two-member pair as `blocked` — the strict direction, with the statement that ran in the entry.

- **Exports — no change at the package doors.** `metadata-protocol`'s `index.ts` is untouched and the package has one entry; `overlay-index.js`'s new names and `historyRowsOfMember` are not re-exported. `SysMetadataRepository`'s option bags gain an optional `member` (additive). `metadata-core`'s `SysMetadataObject` gains a field and an index column (additive). `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` is untouched; `PUT` stays body-addressed; `?locale=` is untouched.

- **The ruling's pins, on the head:** two locales then a restart each serve their own wording (`environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts` on the real engine and protocol; the showcase dogfood on a real SQLite file with real `sendTemplate` and a cold boot); a single-locale save unchanged (one row, member NULL, the other locale on the package wording); a package-shipped bundle unchanged across a restart; a bare-name read answers the canonical member; a duplicate `(type, name, member)` save refused by the index with `UNIQUE constraint failed` on real SQLite, the canonical NULL folded to one bucket; every other type's rows byte-identical before and after the backfill and the rebuild. The ablation the PR records removed the member from the write head and reddened exactly the three member pins while both CONTROLs stayed green.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset names `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/metadata-core` at `patch`; `Clause-②: no` is PR body line 2, the changeset's declaration and the claim's. True for stage 1: no door accepts a new key or parameter; the save door's body-addressed `PUT` is unchanged; the only behavioural movement is the store keeping a second member it used to replace. Stage 2's selector is the widening, not this PR. Patch fits a fix in released packages; the added column and the option bags are not an authorable surface.
- Packages: the diff also changes `@objectstack/platform-objects`' generated bundles — a published package the changeset does not name. All three packages are in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, so they version together whatever the changeset lists; the omission changes nothing in what publishes or at which version, and leaves only the platform-objects CHANGELOG without a line for the regenerated bundles. A note, not a defect in the level.
- Narrowing: none. The index replacement is a relaxation and cannot refuse a store that booted before; the conflict class it still reports pre-dates this PR. The backfill never throws. The pre-flight lists and never refuses, erring only strict. No ADR-0087 marker is owed. On the fallback dialect, one request shape — a second member's save — is refused by the surviving four-column declared index until the operator rebuilds it; that is a refused save where the store previously accepted and lost, not a deployment refusal, and it belongs in the changeset text (see ①), not in a marker.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Seat answer Q1 (sequencing A) — right against the ruling**, which dispatches "two steps (or two PRs)" and gives the migration half the contract-tier review either way. **The window stage 1 leaves:** a non-canonical member is written by a save naming its locale and served by the layered list and the send path, but with no selector it cannot be reset, have its draft published, or be read, diffed or reverted by name until stage 2's selector lands; a pre-fix second-locale row, once backfilled, is no longer removed by a bare `DELETE`. **The changeset states it in substance** — a by-name reset removes the `en-US` customisation only; read, publish, history and revert by name address the `en-US` member; a non-`en-US` customisation is reached through the list and replaced by a save naming its locale — without naming the by-name selector as the closer. One sentence would complete it.
- **Seat answer Q2 (shared counter A) — right**, as judged in ①: a reading within the ruling, not a change to it.
- **The premise half-false** (the registry's bare read answers its overlay tier first): verified in `SchemaRegistry.getItem`; the protocol carries the operative half; `objectql/registry.ts` is untouched; carried to stage 2 together with the member-aware registry heal.
- **`runtime-index-preflight.ts` outside the claim's listed files:** same package, same directory, same lane; one function (`runProbe`) and one private table; the statements themselves live in `overlay-index.ts`, as that module's ownership rule demands; without the edit `os migrate duplicates` answers `unreadable` on every store this version has not booted. Accepted as an in-lane deviation; the adopting seat accepts it by adopting this record.
- **The `domain:cli` census row** (`packages/types/src/driver-error-classification.callers.test.ts`): the frozen enumeration of `operatorFacingErrorText` callers, whose own header makes the PR that adds a caller add its row and its pin; one row, additions only, the pin in `metadata-protocol`. Acceptable on its merits. The claim on the card does not pre-name this edit class, so it is judged here rather than taken from the dispatch.
- **The untranslated bundle keys:** the English fill in `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` is the generator's merge-mode output, recorded in the source-hash companions and accepted by the i18n gates on the head; the two strings are a system table's field label and help. Translation is owed to the `area:i18n` lane as a follow-up; not a stage-1 blocker.
- **Dev findings carried to stage 2, verified:** `removeRuntimeShadow` sweeps a bundle's whole bare group on a by-name reset (its own comment says the overlay layer is keyed by name alone — the premise this PR retires); the other member's row stays, and the list and the send path read the store, as the reset pin shows. `applyRemoteMetadataMutation` re-reads through `repo.get`, so a cluster peer hydrates the canonical member for a non-canonical mutation until its next boot; the package-batch doors address the canonical member. The `driver-sql` drift fixture stays valid: recognition is by the partial predicate, not the part count.
- **First-stage deviations** (the version counter, history rows without a member column, the merge of `main`, the pre-existing branch ref, the lock-discipline slip, the model-free trailers): answered above, or process-only with no bearing on the diff. **Patch-round deviations** (the strict direction; the PR body edits owed): the seat's refreshed body carries the member-less-listing bullet, the head's evidence and the acceptance notes.
- **First-dev report (6113736478):** its two questions were answered by the ruling; its folded finding (a bare-name read serving the second locale) is fixed and pinned here; its `translation` note stands.
- **Notes for the adopting seat, none blocking:** (a) add the fallback-dialect residual to the PR body and the changeset; (b) ADR-0005's present-tense amendment still spells the current key as four parts — the maintainer's 「同意」 on A is the decision's provenance, and an amendment line is Tier H, the maintainer's hand: file it; (c) `origin/main` moved on `protocol.ts` and `sys-metadata-repository.ts` since the merge base (GitHub reports the PR mergeable) — the queue rebuilds, and a merge of `main` before arming is multi-agent §10's own rule; (d) the PR stays draft and waits on #22966 and #22949 for arming, as the seat's CI comment says; the review itself is not blocked by those two steps.

Adopted by `domain:engine#2` (`session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`) at 2026-10-12T06:59Z. The record came from an isolated at-tier reviewer. Its transcript shows read-only tool use: REST reads, a fetch into a review ref and repository reads, and its only write was its own scratch record. The seat accepts the `runtime-index-preflight.ts` edit as an in-lane deviation, as the record judges. **Before arming, the seat acts on the record's notes:**
- (a) and the ③ window: a patch round adds two sentences to the changeset. One gives the fallback-dialect residual: on a driver without partial indexes, a store that booted before keeps its four-column declared UNIQUE, so a second member's save is refused until the operator rebuilds it.
  > ⚠️ **Correction** · seat 2 · 2026-10-12T07:46Z: patch round 2's measurement (6119963033) falsifies the "refused" part, in this note and in the record's ① and ②. Metadata-door rows store no organization, and the four-column UNIQUE never collides NULLs, so on that dialect two members coexist and no save is refused. The changeset now states the verified behaviour, and the delta record on the next head adjudicates it. The other names stage 2's by-name selector as what closes the reset and publish window.
- (c): the same round merges `origin/main` once. The PR body carries the residual too. A delta record follows on that head.
- (b): ADR-0005's four-part key spelling is Tier H, the maintainer's hand. It is filed at landing, when it becomes false on `main`.
- (d): arming waits for a green head, after the `domain:devx` change ruled on #22949 (6119186511) lands.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4d6105d8baa931a5e0731218aebbd96578430556`
Local-runs: none

Delta record on the head above, following the PASS record 6119363786 on `f21b6f9d24`. Reviewed: card #22877 (body and all 14 comments; ruling 6116165299 binding; patch-round reports 6119103318 and 6119963033), PR #22954 (body with the seat's re-edited fallback-dialect bullet, its three comments including the prior record and the seat's correction on its adoption note, the 24-file list), the delta `f21b6f9d24..4d6105d8ba`, the net diff against `main` at the new merge base `246edf5b39`, the head's check-runs, and the `origin/main` files the brief lists. Where this record is silent, the prior record's judgment stands; where it speaks on the fallback dialect, it supersedes the prior record.

**Gates on the head, at the final read:** 42 check-runs, all completed, none pending: 35 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 2 `failure`.
